subject: RFI: offline patch & cryptographic signature workflow for air-gapped deployments
messages:
From: Elena Morales <security@novacare.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-05-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFI: offline patching + signed firmware for air-gapped clusters

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking this RFI. We're evaluating vendors for a fully air-gapped private deployment and need a clear, testable workflow for urgent security patching and long-term maintenance. Specifically we need details on:

- How your team delivers signed software artifacts to an offline customer environment (manifest, binary, SBOM and detached signature).
- How customers verify cryptographic signatures without internet access (recommended key formats, verification tools, sample commands).
- Key rotation / escrow options for offline KMS/HSMs and whether Redwood supports a transfer ceremony.
- Rollback and emergency hotfix procedure for zero-touch operator environments.
- Evidence we can include in our SOC/process documentation (sample signed manifests, example verification logs).

Can you provide a concise workflow and any sample artifacts? We're on a tight procurement timeline and will include this in our security questionnaire.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Director, Security & Compliance
Novacare Health

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <security@novacare.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-03T12:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: offline patching + signed firmware for air-gapped clusters

Elena —

Appreciate the clear list. We have a formal offline patch + signature workflow used for several healthcare and industrial customers; attaching the condensed workflow and a sample key-rotation text file for your procurement pack. High-level summary below and a short playbook in the attachment (offline-patch-workflow.pdf).

Summary (short):
1) Build & sign: We produce artifacts (binary, container, SBOM) and create a detached ECDSA signature (P-384) plus SHA-256 checksums. Signatures are generated from our code-signing HSM.
2) Manifest & SBOM: We publish a signed manifest.json (artifact list, checksums, SBOM V1) and an accompanying signature.asc file.
3) Offline transfer: For air-gapped installs we offer two delivery patterns:
   - Media transfer: encrypted USB or signed ISO shipped via customer logistics (customer controls chain-of-custody).
   - Customer pull: a staged transfer host inside a secured DMZ pulls artifacts; host is then physically transported to air-gapped network.
4) Verification: We include a small verification utility (go binary) with instructions and sample commands (open-source) — runs entirely offline, verifies checksums and signature against the stored customer public key.
5) Keying option: Customers can either:
   - Import Redwood's public verification key into their offline KMS/HSM (recommended), or
   - Use a customer-supplied key pair and have Redwood sign artifacts with the customer's public key (we support customer-supplied signing certificates under an attestation agreement).
6) Rotation: We provide a documented rotation ceremony (sample steps in signature-key-rotation-sample.txt). Rotation is done quarterly or on-compromise, and involves escrowed recovery keys kept in a double-key HSM model for offline retrieval.
7) Emergency hotfix: For critical CVEs we support a signed 'hotfix manifest' with explicit rollback instructions. Operators run the verifier, apply the hotfix, and the runtime checks a detached manifest before activating changes.

Evidence & compliance artifacts included in the attachment: signed manifest example, sample verification log, SBOM extract, and the rotation ceremony checklist. If you want, we can also provide a short recorded demo of the offline verification process.

Attachments: offline-patch-workflow.pdf (playbook), signature-key-rotation-sample.txt (ceremony checklist)

Next steps: If this looks good, can we schedule a 45-minute technical session with your ops/security team this week? Irene (cc'd) will host and can bring the engineering runbook.

Best,
Naomi Feldman

Thanks Naomi — this is helpful. A few clarifications so we can mark compliance items in our questionnaire:

1) For the verification utility, can you confirm supported signature algorithms and whether it validates certificate chains (OCSP/CRL)? We need offline validation guidance.
2) Does Redwood provide a signed firmware image (for third-party appliances) or only application-level artifacts?
3) On key escrow: if we import Redwood's public key, how is compromise handled if Redwood's signing key is suspected to be compromised? Do you have an emergency key revocation and re-sign process that works offline?
4) Do you provide automated verification logs in a standard format (e.g., JSON) that we can ingest into our internal audit repository?

If you can respond to these four points we can close a block in the RFI. Also please confirm whether you can attend a review call on Friday 2028-05-05 at 10:00 PT.

Elena

Hi Elena —

Answers inline:

1) Verification utility: supports ECDSA P-256 and P-384, RSA-2048, and SHA-256 checksums. For offline validation we provide certificate chain bundles (PEM) and the verifier performs chain validation against the supplied bundle. OCSP/CRL are optional online checks; for air-gapped sites the recommended pattern is an "offline revocation list" (we publish signed revocation manifests with timestamps that the verifier checks).

2) Signed firmware images: we can sign third-party appliance images provided we have an integration agreement and a reproducible build hash. We produce both application-level artifacts and, under a suitable agreement, firmware images and signed bootloader payloads.

3) Compromise handling: emergency path is documented in rotation-file and playbook — short summary:
   - Redwood publishes a signed "revocation manifest" (detached and timestamped) and communicates via pre-agreed channel.
   - Customers using Redwood's public key import the revocation manifest into their offline verifier to reject new artifacts signed by the compromised key.
   - We provide a transition kit: new key pair, signed transitioning manifests (signed by both old and new keys when possible), and step-by-step operator actions. For completely offline customers we provide a sealed transition media and a documented double-witness key ceremony.

4) Verification logs: yes — verifier emits structured JSON logs (timestamp, manifest-id, artifact-hash, verification-result, operator-id) and a human-friendly text summary. Logs can be exported via a signed archive for ingestion into your audit system. Sample verification log included in the PDF attachment.

Call: Friday 2028-05-05 10:00 PT works for our team. Irene will lead the runbook walkthrough and Ben will cover keying/rotation details. We'll send a calendar invite and include a short demo video link in the calendar.

Attachments in this email: operator-runbook-v1.md (operator steps + commands)

Looking forward to the call — let us know if you want us to redact any sensitive examples from the attachments before sharing more broadly.

Best regards,
Naomi Feldman
